scenarios.title: Bring two switch links into one working group
scenarios.summary: Bring two passive links into a verified two-member VLAN trunk.
scenarios.objective: Campus A and Campus B have two cables, p1 and p2, assigned to bundle. Bring both pairs into the group and carry VLANs 10 and 20. Keep operations and its p7/p8 links, and both VLAN databases, unchanged.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the first member exclusion, then the relevant local port/group. A participating bundle does not prove that both VLANs pass. Apply before checking.
steps: Inspect each end of p1 and p2: local group, line profile and LACP mode.
Change enough initiation modes for both cable pairs to negotiate. Apply configuration.
Check both participating pairs and both VLAN services; preserve operations.
scenarios.explanation: A passive port can answer but does not start this modeled LACP agreement. Each p1/p2 cable needs an active end; Active/Passive and Active/Active both work. Only compatible ports participate. VLAN admission is checked separately. Matching group names alone do not prove that a bundle formed.
hints: Local group membership selects a logical bundle. Physical peers are fixed by supplied cables.
Each required pair needs an active end, compatible rates, full duplex and locally matching group profiles.
Inspect required VLANs separately. Repair allowed lists consistently on each group and its members; preserve operations.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded Layer 2 LACP eligibility and logical VLAN admission on supplied switches. Native configuration controls are simulator tools, not Cisco IOS commands. No PDUs, negotiation timers, real traffic, throughput/load-balancing, routed EtherChannel, spanning-tree composition or platform-specific partner-selection tie-break. Only declared cable-loss cases are modeled.

etherchannel_teaching.prerequisite_note: Before starting: review the VLAN trunk lesson. A trunk carries listed VLANs; the native VLAN is distinct from allowed data VLANs. This lesson introduces combining compatible links.

concepts.title: Several cables, one useful connection
concepts.text: A bundle groups compatible physical links between two switches. Each switch has its own local group and member settings. Matching group names alone do not prove that any cables joined.

concepts.title: Start, match, then carry data
concepts.text: Active starts LACP negotiation; Passive responds. A cable needs an active end. A member also needs its own group’s line rate and VLAN profile, compatible cable-end rates, and full duplex. A participating bundle still needs each data VLAN active and allowed at both ends.

concepts.title: Edit, apply and verify
concepts.text: Choose a switch, edit group or physical-member rows, then Apply configuration. The applied-network view reports resulting state. Check configuration verifies the whole assignment, including preserved links. Fields and applied state are saved separately.

etherchannel_teaching.example_description: In the separate example, p1 and p2 are passive at both ends. Make both cable pairs participate and carry VLANs 40 and 50. This example never earns assignment credit.

example_actions.title: Prepare the worked example configuration
example_actions.explanation: Fill sets example-a p1 and p2 to Active and leaves example-b Passive, keeping other settings. Each pair can then negotiate. Fill prepares fields only: inspect the modes, Apply configuration, then Check configuration.

try_change.description: After the example passes, turn off Up for example-a p1. Apply and Check to observe how losing a member affects required outcomes. Re-enable it, Apply and Check to recover. This changes only the separate example.

scenarios.title: Restore members and the missing data VLAN
scenarios.summary: Separate local member compatibility from end-to-end VLAN admission.
scenarios.objective: The distribution bundle should carry VLANs 10 and 20 across p1 and p2. Diagnose an excluded member and the data VLAN still blocked after members join. Restore both services while preserving operations, p7/p8, and both VLAN databases.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the first member exclusion, then the relevant local port/group. A participating bundle does not prove that both VLANs pass. Apply before checking.
steps: Compare each excluded port with its own group template.
Repair local profile consistency, apply, then inspect each VLAN service separately.
Repair the missing allowed VLAN on the relevant group and its members; apply and check without altering operations.
scenarios.explanation: A member must match its own local group template. A correct remote port cannot fix a local profile mismatch. A participating bundle can still exclude a required VLAN. Keep each local template and its member profiles consistent, and allow both required VLANs at both ends. Additional allowed VLANs from the supplied database are a valid alternative.
hints: Local group membership selects a logical bundle. Physical peers are fixed by supplied cables.
Each required pair needs an active end, compatible rates, full duplex and locally matching group profiles.
Inspect required VLANs separately. Repair allowed lists consistently on each group and its members; preserve operations.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded Layer 2 LACP eligibility and logical VLAN admission on supplied switches. Native configuration controls are simulator tools, not Cisco IOS commands. No PDUs, negotiation timers, real traffic, throughput/load-balancing, routed EtherChannel, spanning-tree composition or platform-specific partner-selection tie-break. Only declared cable-loss cases are modeled.

example_actions.title: Prepare the worked example configuration
example_actions.explanation: Fill repairs the local member profile and the remote trunk’s missing second VLAN, including matching member profiles. Inspect group and port details, Apply, then check membership and each VLAN independently.

scenarios.title: Move a bundle without losing its spare path
scenarios.summary: Migrate a bundle, prove single-link resilience, and preserve a neighboring service.
scenarios.objective: Move p1–p4 out of previous and build bundle with at least three participating pairs. VLANs 10 and 20 must work now and retain at least two pairs if any supplied member cable fails. Empty previous on both switches; preserve operations, p7/p8 and both VLAN databases.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the first member exclusion, then the relevant local port/group. A participating bundle does not prove that both VLANs pass. Apply before checking.
steps: Inspect old membership and the new bundle templates.
Move at least three compatible p1–p4 pairs into bundle and clear previous on both ends.
Inspect every supplied cable-loss calculation, then Check all current, failure and preservation outcomes.
scenarios.explanation: Three participating pairs leave two when one fails; four is also valid. Each supplied cable-loss state is evaluated independently of current service. Clearing previous proves a completed migration. Preserving operations prevents fixing the target by damaging a neighboring service.
hints: Local group membership selects a logical bundle. Physical peers are fixed by supplied cables.
Each required pair needs an active end, compatible rates, full duplex and locally matching group profiles.
Inspect required VLANs separately. Repair allowed lists consistently on each group and its members; preserve operations.
For every supplied cable loss, two pairs and both data VLANs must remain. Clear previous membership on both switches.

concepts.title: Prove the spare path
concepts.text: A supplied single-link failure is calculated without changing saved cables. Three participating pairs leave two after one fails. A working current bundle does not prove each failure case. A migration must remove old membership as well as create the new group.

etherchannel_teaching.example_description: In the separate example, move at least three p1–p4 pairs into demo-bundle, clear demo-previous, and preserve demo-operations. Inspect the supplied cable-loss cases.

example_actions.title: Prepare the worked example configuration
example_actions.explanation: Fill moves p1–p3 into demo-bundle at both ends with compatible profiles and leaves p4 unbundled. Three pairs leave two under each supplied single-cable loss. It clears demo-previous and preserves demo-operations. Inspect, Apply and Check.
